A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Decoupled SGDA work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices G–H report original optimization experiments, noise comparisons, Ghost Sequence results, and GAN training results on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.

after.justification: The same original experimental outcomes remain in Section 5 and Appendices G–H, including convergence curves and GAN FID measurements, despite the new Impact Statement describing the work as purely theoretical.

M1.justification: The proposed updates and Algorithms 1–4 are retained, including the multiplayer, federated, and Ghost Sequence extensions. Ghost-SGDA is a new shorthand for the existing heuristic, not a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate quadratic games, the nonconvex toy GAN, imbalanced gradient-noise scenarios, and GAN training on CIFAR-10 and SVHN. Appendix experiments retain the same task and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PEARL-SGD as an analytical communication-complexity comparator, with an explicit comparison in new Remark 4.6. This is a theoretical comparison; the methods actually run in the empirical experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix I retains the same experimental settings, including coupling sweeps, local-step counts, accuracy thresholds, communication budgets, GAN training settings, and FID evaluation procedure. No new experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The local-step and coupling analyses, noise sensitivity experiments, Ghost Sequence comparison, and supplementary trajectories are retained. Figures 8–10 already appeared in v1; their placement changes do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Appendices I.2–I.3 retain the five-trial averaging descriptions, and the plotted uncertainty shading is preserved. No new seed information, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports PEARL-SGD communication bounds of κ² log(1/ε) in both complexity columns, supported by the new analytical comparison in Remark 4.6. Existing empirical curves, rankings, and findings in Figures 1–5 and 8–10 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Lemma B.3 supplies a proof connecting Lc = 0 to fully decoupled objectives. Remark 4.6 adds reasoning comparing star-cocoercivity-based communication bounds with the coupling-sensitive analysis. The central convergence guarantees and existing multiplayer, quadratic, and federated proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens novelty wording to the first method designed for ISC-games and explicitly presents the coupling assumptions as a contribution. The principal communication-acceleration and noise-robustness claims remain; the expanded Ghost-SGDA contribution summarizes material already in v1.

C2.justification: Remark 4.6 adds a substantive explanation of the claimed advantage over PEARL-SGD: its bounds retain conditioning dependence, whereas the separate coupling parameter captures weak interaction. Existing interpretations of the empirical results and the Ghost heuristic are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Appendix I retains the same implementation and reproducibility information, including architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, CUDA, and NVIDIA L4 hardware. Algorithm 1 makes previously documented inputs more explicit without introducing new technical settings or access information.

R1.justification: Yoon et al. (2025), already cited in v1, is repositioned as independent concurrent work and compared explicitly through PEARL-SGD. v2 also adds references on decentralized multi-agent learning, distributed variational inequalities, star-cocoercivity, and the authors' earlier workshop version.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion are revised; explanatory passages and experiment subsection headings are refined. Impact and acknowledgment sections are added, while the populated contents list disappears. The overall section sequence and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Plot labels are reformatted, Figures 4–5 become much smaller, and Table 1 gains a comparator row. Existing experimental displays are preserved rather than replaced with new results.

improvement.justification: The explicit zero-coupling proof and focused comparison with closely related PEARL-SGD make the theoretical contribution easier to assess than in v1. These are limited gains because the main guarantees and experimental evidence are retained. The new layout has drawbacks, particularly smaller Figures 4–5 and the missing contents entries, but the added theoretical explanation and positioning provide a modest overall improvement.
